definition: Tariffs are the public rate documents pipelines file describing their transportation charges; volume is the quantity of gas moved; zones are the geographic segments a pipeline is divided into for rate-setting purposes.
core_idea: Pipeline transportation pricing is publicly documented (tariffs) and can vary by geographic segment of the pipeline (zones) rather than being uniform end to end.
key_points: Tariffs are commonly public and can be found on the pipeline's own site or the relevant regulator's site (e.g., the eFERC site in the U.S.).
Volume refers simply to the quantity of gas transported.
Zones divide a pipeline into different geographic areas that can carry different rates; a 'postage stamp' pipeline is the special case of just one zone.
relationships: Zones are the mechanism by which a pipeline can charge differently from a simple single postage-stamp rate.
trading_implications: Traders can look up actual pipeline rates directly from filed tariffs rather than relying on estimates.
